subject: QuickServe pilot: Tokenflow SLO capture and sizing next steps
messages:
From: David Kim <david@redwood.com>
To: Lina Park <lina@quickserve.com>; Evan Moore <evan@quickserve.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QuickServe pilot: tokenflow SLO capture and sizing next steps

Hi Lina / Evan —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we captured and the immediate asks so our infra and SRE teams can map to a pilot sizing: 

Key workload characteristics (need confirmation):
- Request mix: 60% streaming (progressive responses), 40% non-streaming completions.
- Steady-state QPS you mentioned ~20–30 QPS, with short spikes. We need explicit peak windows (duration) to convert to tokens/sec.
- Average tokens per full request: ~400–550 tokens (please confirm distribution / 90th pct).
- Typical session length / context: 2–3 turns, ~3k token context max.
- Latency targets: streaming P95 target ~250–350ms, non-streaming completion P99 target ~900–1200ms (to be validated).

Open questions / asks from Redwood ops to finalize sizing:
1) Can you share a 24–48h sample of request logs (anonymized) or a tokens-per-request histogram? That lets us compute tokens/sec and realistic batching efficiency. (Attached is a small template: qs-token-sample-100k.json)
2) What is your definition of a "peak"? Example: 5-minute window at X QPS vs 1-minute burst. Please provide both avg peak-window QPS and longest sustained peak.
3) For streaming requests: are they long-lived dependencies (server-sent events) or short continuous chunks? We need average tokens produced per streaming request and how often clients cancel early.
4) Any hard SLAs or audit constraints that require dedicated capacity (e.g., P95 < 300ms is a contractual target)?

Initial sizing guidance we discussed on-call (rough):
- If peak 1-min QPS <= 200 with avg tokens 450 -> pilot: 1 dedicated 80GB GPU node (optimized dynamic batching + KV cache) + 1 burst node.
- If peak > 400 QPS or streaming > 65% with low-latency P95 < 300ms -> recommend 2 reserved nodes and a streaming-optimized inference path.

Next steps I propose:
- You upload the sample logs or complete the small template (attached) by EOD Thu 3/18.
- Redwood runs a quick tokens/sec and QPS conversion and returns a compact pilot matrix (I’ll loop Marissa + Karthik for sizing).
- Schedule a 45-min sizing workshop to finalize pilot config (I’m available Tue/Wed next week).

Attachments: qs-token-sample-100k.json (template), pilot-matrix.xlsx (blank) — please attach any traffic dumps as gzipped JSON if large.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: QuickServe pilot: tokenflow SLO capture and sizing next steps

David —

Thanks for the clear recap. We validated a few numbers from our side and attached two items: a 24h anonymized sample (qs-token-sample-100k.json) and a short pilot constraints sheet. Highlights: 

- Steady-state: 25 QPS (1 hour moving avg).
- Peak bursts: short 1–3 minute spikes up to 320 QPS, occasional daily burst up to 420 QPS (rare, ~2x/week).
- Tokens per request: median 380, mean 455, 90th percentile 820.
- Streaming: ~62% of requests are streaming. For streaming sessions average produced tokens = 230 (clients often cut early); 95th pct produced ~680.
- Typical longest sustained peak we care about is a 5-minute window.
- Context length: up to 4k tokens (we plan to keep context trimmed to last 2–3 turns in production).
- Hard SLA ask: customer-facing checkout flows require P95 latency <= 300ms for streaming responses during pilot. Non-streaming has softer goals (P99 <= 1s).

We attached the sample and pilot-matrix.xlsx filled with our rough numbers. Evan and I are available for a sizing workshop Wed 3/17 or Thu 3/18 morning.

Attachments: qs-token-sample-100k.json, pilot-matrix.xlsx

—
Lina Park
Sr. Eng Manager, QuickServe

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Park <lina@quickserve.com>, Evan Moore <evan@quickserve.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QuickServe pilot: tokenflow SLO capture and sizing next steps

Adding some ops-level notes after reviewing the sample: 

- Conversions we ran locally: with mean tokens ~455 and 5-min peak 320 QPS -> peak token/sec ~= 145,600 tokens/sec. That’s the key figure for batching efficiency calculations.
- Streaming mix (62%) with average produced tokens 230 means streaming token emission rate during bursts matters more than request QPS alone — we should model token-emission windows separately.
- Context/kv cache: with 4k context we recommend enabling prefix caching for stable session prefixes. Please confirm whether customer will provide a session key per user to leverage KV cache.
- Concurrency expectations: during the 1–3 minute spikes we observed concurrency of ~8–12 requests active per second per session bucket; that impacts concurrency slots for the runtime.

Preliminary pilot config suggestion (internal):
- Start pilot with: 2 x 80GB-class nodes (reserved) with streaming-optimized runtime; 1 x 80GB burst node for peak absorb.
- Batching / tokenization: configure small max-batch latency for streaming path (5–10ms) and larger batch for non-streaming (30–50ms) to improve throughput.
- Canary: route 10% of checkout traffic in canary for 48h, measure P95 streaming and the token emission tail.

Action items for David / Marissa:
- Confirm whether QuickServe can surface a stable session key (for KV cache).
- Confirm workshop time (Wed/Thu morning).
- We’ll produce a compact pilot matrix with cost, expected P95/P99, and fallback policy options.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Perfect, thanks for the fast turnaround and the sample data. We’ve ingested the sample and Karthik’s numbers look right. I’ve penciled in a 45-min sizing workshop for Thu 3/18 at 10:00 AM PT (invite sent). Agenda:

1) Walk the tokens/sec conversion and burst windows (10m)
2) Pilot topology and reserved vs burst nodes
3) Streaming path: batching latency settings and canary plan
4) Data/attachment handoff: confirm S3/GCS upload for larger dumps

Quick asks before the workshop: please confirm whether QuickServe can provide a session id key in the request headers (used for KV cache) and whether you expect clients to cancel streaming mid-response >20% of the time.

If anything changes to the workshop time, shout — otherwise see you Thu.
